{{nihongo|'''Heda Shrine'''|部田神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Izu Province]].

'''Heda Shrine''' (Heda Jinja) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} located in {{ill|Heda, Shizuoka|Q5697064|qid=Q5697064|lt=Heda}}, {{ill|Numazu|ar|نامازو (شيزوكا)|arz|نامازو|azb|نومازو، شیزوئوکا|bg|Нумадзу|ce|Нумадзу|ceb|Numazu (lungsod sa Hapon)|de|Numazu|eo|Numazu|es|Numazu (Shizuoka)|et|Numazu|fa|نومازو، شیزوئوکا|fi|Numazu|fr|Numazu|ga|Numazu|gl|Numazu|hr|Numazu|id|Numazu, Shizuoka|io|Numazu, Shizuoka|it|Numazu|ja|沼津市|ko|누마즈시|mg|Numazu|mn|Нүмазү|mzn|نومازو، شیزوئوکا|nl|Numazu|no|Numazu|pl|Numazu|pt|Numazu|ro|Numazu|ru|Нумадзу|sh|Numazu|simple|Numazu|sr|Нумазу|sv|Numazu|szl|Numazu|tg|Нумазу|th|นูมาซุ|tl|Numazu|tr|Numazu|tt|Нумадзу|uk|Нумадзу (Сідзуока)|ur|نومازو، شیزوکا|vi|Numazu, Shizuoka|war|Numazu, Shizuoka|zh|沼津市|zh_classical|沼津市|zh_min_nan|Numazu-chhī|zh_yue|沼津|qid=Q241037}}, {{ill|Shizuoka Prefecture|Q131320|qid=Q131320}}. It is the local tutelary shrine (ujigami) of the area and is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}}.

=== Enshrined deity ===
* '''{{ill|Ōkuninushi|Q276944|qid=Q276944|lt=Ōkuninushi-no-Mikoto}}'''
Formerly known as Buta-gami, Buta-no-za-gami, and Heta no Myōjin, it was an {{ill|Ubusunagami|Q1392097|qid=Q1392097}} (local ancestral deity). In ancient times it was an object of {{ill|Prince Shōtoku|Q263972|qid=Q263972}} worship ({{ill|Taishi cult|Q112695190|qid=Q112695190}}), but as of the 21st century the principal enshrined deity is Ōkuninushi-no-Mikoto.<ref name="戸田村史通史編141p"/>

=== History ===
The date of foundation is unknown. It is the Shikinaisha “Buta Shrine” listed in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|abstract|Q11064932|fr|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|simple|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|zh|延喜式神名帳|qid=Q11064932}} and has a history of over 1,000 years.<ref name="戸田村史民俗偏344p"/> While {{ill|Morokuchi Shrine (Q116694076)|Q116694076|qid=Q116694076}} on {{ill|Cape Mihama|Q11489198|qid=Q11489198}} is said to protect Heda from the sea, this shrine is regarded as the tutelary deity protecting it from the mountain side, and toward the end of the Edo period it was also called “Mishima Myōjin.”<ref name="戸田村史民俗偏344p"/><ref name="戸田村史通史編141p">{{Cite book|Japanese|author=Editorial Committee of the History of Toda Village |title=History of Toda Village: General History |publisher=Numazu City |date=2016 |page=141 |isbn=}}</ref><ref name="玄松子"/> In the Izu Province Shrine Rank Register it is recorded as Junior Fourth Rank, Upper Grade, “Heta no Myōjin.”<ref name="玄松子">{{Cite web|Japanese|url=https://www.genbu.net/data/izu/heda_title.htm |title=Heda Shrine |publisher= |accessdate=2020-03-23}}</ref> It was positioned as the general guardian shrine of the West Izu region and worshipped as a god of good fortune and as a protector of agriculture, fishing, and commerce.<ref name="玄松子"/> It is also said that the neighboring Myōhō Renge-ji temple served as the shrine’s bettō (shrine-temple administrator).<ref name="玄松子"/>

Ten ridge plaques dating from 1596 (Keichō 1) to 1823 (Bunsei 6) survive, revealing that at least ten reconstructions and repairs were carried out.<ref name="戸田村史通史編141p"/> In particular, the 1817 (Bunka 14) plaque lists many stewards, including the village headman Katsuro family and newly risen shipping merchants, indicating that the reconstruction took place during a period of prosperity in Heda Village.<ref name="戸田村史通史編142p">{{Cite book|Japanese|author=Editorial Committee of the History of Toda Village |title=History of Toda Village: General History |publisher=Numazu City |date=2016 |page=142 |isbn=}}</ref>

=== Grounds ===
The shrine is located roughly in the center of the Heda valley.<ref name="戸田村史通史編141p"/> According to shrine records, the grounds cover 424 tsubo. Several large trees such as {{ill|Chamaecyparis obtusa|Q917187|qid=Q917187}}, {{ill|Podocarpus macrophyllus|Q165063|qid=Q165063}}, and {{ill|Celtis sinensis|Q706339|qid=Q706339}} grow naturally there. Among them, several large {{ill|Camphora officinarum|Q158722|qid=Q158722}} with distinctive burls have been designated Natural Monuments by Numazu City.<ref name="戸田村史民俗偏344p"/>

=== Shrine buildings ===
* Main hall (Honden) – {{ill|cypress bark roof|Q90373477|qid=Q90373477}}, keyaki-wood {{ill|Nagare-zukuri|Q210684|qid=Q210684}}, housed within a red protective structure.
* Worship hall (Haiden) – Copper roofing, {{ill|East Asian hip-and-gable roof|Q855025|qid=Q855025}}.
* Auxiliary/enshrined shrines (within the precincts)
** Hie Shrine – enshrines {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kumano Kushimikenu no Mikoto}}.
** Hachiman Shrine – enshrines {{ill|Emperor Ōjin|Q317997|qid=Q317997}}.
** Yachimata Shrine – enshrines {{ill|Sarutahiko Ōkami|Q3090037|qid=Q3090037|lt=Sarutahiko-no-Mikoto}}.
* Daijingū – enshrines {{ill|Q?|qid=Q?|lt=Ōhirume no Muchi}}.
* Tatsuta Shrine – enshrines {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Shinatobe no Mikoto}} and {{ill|Shinatsuhiko|Q1073925|qid=Q1073925|lt=Shinatsuhiko no Mikoto}}.
* Chūkonsha – enshrines {{ill|Prince Shōtoku|Q263972|qid=Q263972}}; some sources record it as Umayado Shrine.

=== Festivals ===
The annual festival was formerly held on the 9th and 10th days of the 9th lunar month, but with the calendar reform it became October 9–10, and in recent years has been changed to a Sunday in October.<ref name="戸田村史民俗偏344p">{{Cite book|Japanese|author=Editorial Committee of the History of Toda Village |title=History of Toda Village: Folk Customs |publisher=Numazu City |date=2014 |page=344 |isbn=}}</ref> Eighteen districts take turns handling festival duties; districts with fewer parishioners cooperate, completing one full rotation over a little more than ten years. The main duties of the host districts include making {{ill|Shimenawa|ar|شيميناوا|ca|Shimenawa|cs|Šimenawa|de|Shimenawa|el|Σιμενάουα|es|Shimenawa|fa|شیمه‌ناوا|fi|Shimenawa|fr|Shimenawa|id|Shimenawa|it|Shimenawa|ja|注連縄|jv|Shimenawa|ko|금줄|no|Shimenawa|pl|Shimenawa|pt|Shimenawa|ru|Симэнава|simple|Shimenawa|sr|Шименава|tr|Shimenawa|zh|注連繩|qid=Q1887421}} (sacred ropes) and providing entertainment on the festival day.<ref name="戸田村史民俗偏345p">{{Cite book|Japanese|author=Editorial Committee of the History of Toda Village |title=History of Toda Village: Folk Customs |publisher=Numazu City |date=2014 |page=345 |isbn=}}</ref> Compared with the spring Benten festival held by the fishing association, this has traditionally been a modest festival, without kagura or floats.<ref name="戸田村史民俗偏345p"/>

Each year, the shimenawa are adjusted: three large ropes 3.8 meters long for the torii, worship hall, and sanctuary; one medium rope 2.5 meters long for the Chūkonsha; and four small ropes 1.7 meters long for small shrines, the stage, and the water pavilion.<ref name="戸田村史民俗偏345p"/>

Entertainment is performed on a stage. In the 20th century, when youth groups were active, the precinct office served as the stage, and youths from each branch competed with performances or hired entertainers.<ref name="戸田村史民俗偏345p"/> In the past, stallholders came from {{ill|Numazu|ar|نامازو (شيزوكا)|arz|نامازو|azb|نومازو، شیزوئوکا|bg|Нумадзу|ce|Нумадзу|ceb|Numazu (lungsod sa Hapon)|de|Numazu|eo|Numazu|es|Numazu (Shizuoka)|et|Numazu|fa|نومازو، شیزوئوکا|fi|Numazu|fr|Numazu|ga|Numazu|gl|Numazu|hr|Numazu|id|Numazu, Shizuoka|io|Numazu, Shizuoka|it|Numazu|ja|沼津市|ko|누마즈시|mg|Numazu|mn|Нүмазү|mzn|نومازو، شیزوئوکا|nl|Numazu|no|Numazu|pl|Numazu|pt|Numazu|ro|Numazu|ru|Нумадзу|sh|Numazu|simple|Numazu|sr|Нумазу|sv|Numazu|szl|Numazu|tg|Нумазу|th|นูมาซุ|tl|Numazu|tr|Numazu|tt|Нумадзу|uk|Нумадзу (Сідзуока)|ur|نومازو، شیزوکا|vi|Numazu, Shizuoka|war|Numazu, Shizuoka|zh|沼津市|zh_classical|沼津市|zh_min_nan|Numazu-chhī|zh_yue|沼津|qid=Q241037|lt=Numazu}} to set up booths, and there was even a revolving stage.<ref name="戸田村史民俗偏345p"/> In the 21st century, outside stalls have been reduced, with local chambers of commerce and women’s associations providing booths, songs, and performances.<ref name="戸田村史民俗偏345p"/>

=== Cultural properties ===
[[File:(2)Heda jinjya Kusu, Heda, Shizuoka.jpg|thumb|Large camphor tree with burls. The one in front is regarded as the sacred tree.]]
; Large burl-bearing camphor trees of Heda Shrine
: Two large camphor trees within the precincts were designated Natural Monuments by Numazu City on March 28, 2006 (Heisei 18).<ref name="現地クスノキ">Based on an on-site sign installed in 2008 by the Numazu City Board of Education.</ref> The northern tree (①), regarded as the sacred tree, has a height of 34.5 m, a girth at breast height of 6.7 m, and a root circumference of 12.7 m.<ref name="現地クスノキ"/> The southern tree (②) has a height of 34.2 m, a girth of 6.2 m, and a root circumference of 11.3 m.<ref name="現地クスノキ"/>
; Ema (votive tablets)
: Two ema (paintings) inside the shrine were designated cultural properties by {{ill|Heda, Shizuoka|Q5697064|qid=Q5697064|lt=Heda Village}} on April 21, 1983 (Shōwa 58). They are “Flowers and Birds” dedicated in 1819 (Bunsei 2) and “Heda Fire Brigade I-gumi New Year Parade” painted in 1889 (Meiji 13).

=== On-site information ===
* Address: 〒410-3402 1585 Heda, {{ill|Numazu|ar|نامازو (شيزوكا)|arz|نامازو|azb|نومازو، شیزوئوکا|bg|Нумадзу|ce|Нумадзу|ceb|Numazu (lungsod sa Hapon)|de|Numazu|eo|Numazu|es|Numazu (Shizuoka)|et|Numazu|fa|نومازو، شیزوئوکا|fi|Numazu|fr|Numazu|ga|Numazu|gl|Numazu|hr|Numazu|id|Numazu, Shizuoka|io|Numazu, Shizuoka|it|Numazu|ja|沼津市|ko|누마즈시|mg|Numazu|mn|Нүмазү|mzn|نومازو، شیزوئوکا|nl|Numazu|no|Numazu|pl|Numazu|pt|Numazu|ro|Numazu|ru|Нумадзу|sh|Numazu|simple|Numazu|sr|Нумазу|sv|Numazu|szl|Numazu|tg|Нумазу|th|นูมาซุ|tl|Numazu|tr|Numazu|tt|Нумадзу|uk|Нумадзу (Сідзуока)|ur|نومازو، شیزوکا|vi|Numazu, Shizuoka|war|Numazu, Shizuoka|zh|沼津市|zh_classical|沼津市|zh_min_nan|Numazu-chhī|zh_yue|沼津|qid=Q241037}}, {{ill|Shizuoka Prefecture|Q131320|qid=Q131320}}<ref>{{Cite web|Japanese|url=http://www.shizuoka-jinjacho.or.jp/shokai/jinja.php?id=4402125 |title=Shizuoka Prefecture Association of Shinto Shrines |publisher= |accessdate=2020-03-23}}</ref>
* Access (bus): Get off at “Miya-no-mae,” about a 1-minute walk (46 m), or “JA Heda Branch,” about a 6-minute walk (456 m).<ref>{{Cite web|Japanese|url=https://yaokami.jp/1220998/ |title=Yaoyorozu no Kami |publisher= |accessdate=2020-03-23}}</ref>
It is located about 500 meters east of {{ill|Port of Heda|Q11496540|qid=Q11496540|lt=Heda Port}}, slightly south of {{ill|Shizuoka Prefectural Road Route 18|Q11663339|qid=Q11663339}}, and enshrined facing toward the harbor.<ref name="玄松子"/>
